title: Cross-Cloud Log Ingestion Pipeline Health

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.4.7 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.4.7 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=_internal` sourcetype=`aws:cloudtrail` collected via Splunk _internal, ingest metrics, or custom heartbeat; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
app: Splunk _internal, ingest metrics, or custom heartbeat
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" source=*metrics* group=per_sourcetype_thruput
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress awsRegion

description: Log pipelines (CloudTrail → S3 → Splunk, Event Hub → Splunk, Pub/Sub → Splunk) can break. Monitoring pipeline health ensures no audit or observability gaps.
value: Detecting cross-cloud log ingestion pipeline health early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Track last event time per cloud sourcetype (e.g. aws:cloudtrail, mscs:azure:audit, google:gcp:pubsub). Alert when no events received for >15–30 minutes. Monitor Event Hub consumer lag and Pub/Sub subscription backlog as pipeline indicators.
visualization: Table (sourcetype, last event, delay), Single value (stale pipelines), Timeline (ingest volume by source).
knownFalsePositives: This pattern can surge during change windows, in sandboxes, and when a platform is in maintenance, so we line alerts up with the calendar and take a second look before we call it an incident.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=_internal`.
• Install and configure Splunk _internal, ingest metrics, or custom heartbeat with the modular input for `aws:cloudtrail`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.4.33.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Track last event time per cloud sourcetype (e.g. aws:cloudtrail, mscs:azure:audit, google:gcp:pubsub). Alert when no events received for >15–30 minutes. Monitor Event Hub consumer lag and Pub/Sub subscription backlog as pipeline indicators.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=_internal sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=_internal sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" source=*metrics* group=per_sourcetype_thruput
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress awsRegion
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.4.7_cross_cloud_log_ingestio_7"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudtrail` in `index=_internal` to detect cross-cloud log ingestion pipeline health. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the AWS CloudTrail console Event history for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_4_7_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Table (sourcetype, last event, delay), Single value (stale pipelines), Timeline (ingest volume by source)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade Splunk _internal, ingest metrics, or custom heartbeat and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of cross-cloud log ingestion pipeline health so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
